title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يشارك في اجتماع مجلس أمناء الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين في الدوحة
title_en: His Eminence the Sheikh Takes Part in the Meeting of the Board of Trustees of the International Union of Muslim Scholars in Doha
body_ar:
شارك الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء – بوصفه عضوا في الاتحاد - في الاجتماع الثالث من الدورة الثالثة لمجلس أمناء الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين المنعقد في مدينة الدوحة 08-09 محرم 1433 هـ / 03 – 04 ديسمبر 2011م.

وشارك في هذا الاجتماع ثلاثون عضواً عالجوا فيه العديد من القضايا الإدارية والهيكلية وناقشوا عددا من قضايا ومشاكل العالم الإسلامي، وناقشوا جدول أعمالهم وبعد المناقشة والتحاور أصدروا عدداً من القرارات والتوصيات، وختموا اجتماعهم بإصدار بيان ختامي ركزوا فيه على بيان موقف الاتحاد من الثورات التي اجتاحت الوطن العربي، ووجهوا رسائل بخصوص الأقطار التي نجحت فيها الثورات والتي لا تزال في الطريق بإذن الله.

ويتلخص بيان الاتحاد الذي أصدره بخصوص ثورات الربيع العربي فيما يلي:

1- أن التغيير والنصر من عند الله وهو وحده المستحق بالحمد والثناء.

2- إخلاص النية لله وحده وتوحيد الصفوف لخدمة الدين والأمة.

3- ينبغي للذين يتهيؤون للمناصب القيادية في تلك البلدان أن يتقوا الله ولا يغرنهم بريق السلطة والمناصب الزائلة.

4- تقبُّل حقيقة التعددية التي هي من سنن الله ونواميسه في الكون.

5- تأمُّل سنن الله في الكون ومنها سنة التدرج في إصلاح ما فسد في الأحقاب الماضية من الظلم والاستبداد.

6- اعتبار الأولويات وعدم الاشتغال بالفروع دون الأصول وبالمهم دون الأهم.

7- من أهم الأمور تحقيق الوحدة الوطنية في كل قطر والتعاون بين الأقطار لتحقيق التنمية الشاملة والمستدامة.

وأخيرا أعرب الاتحاد عن مواصلة عزمه على ترشيد الأمة وتصحيح مفاهيمها ودفعها إلى النهضة الحضارية المنشودة.

للاطلاع على البيان الختامي اضغط هنا:
body_en:
Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, took part — in his capacity as a member of the Union — in the third meeting of the third session of the board of trustees of the International Union of Muslim Scholars, held in the city of Doha on 08–09 Muharram 1433 AH / 03–04 December 2011 CE.

Thirty members took part in this meeting, in which they dealt with many administrative and structural questions and discussed a number of the issues and problems of the Muslim world. They discussed their agenda, and after discussion and deliberation issued a number of decisions and recommendations, and closed their meeting by issuing a final communiqué, in which they concentrated on setting out the Union's position on the revolutions that have swept the Arab world, and addressed messages concerning the countries in which the revolutions have succeeded and those still on the way, God willing.

The Union's communiqué on the revolutions of the Arab Spring may be summarised as follows:

1. That change and victory are from God, and He alone deserves praise and commendation.

2. Sincerity of intention (niyyah) to God alone, and the unifying of the ranks in the service of the religion and of the community.

3. Those who are preparing themselves for leading positions in those countries ought to be mindful of God, and not to be deceived by the glitter of power and of passing office.

4. Accepting the fact of plurality, which is among God's established patterns and laws in the created order.

5. Contemplating God's established patterns in the created order, among them the pattern of gradualness in reforming the oppression and despotism that went wrong in ages past.

6. Regard for priorities, and not occupying oneself with subsidiary matters to the neglect of fundamentals, or with the important to the neglect of the more important.

7. Among the most important matters is the achieving of national unity in each country, and cooperation between countries to achieve comprehensive and sustainable development.

Finally the Union expressed its continuing determination to guide the community rightly, to correct its concepts, and to drive it towards the sought-after civilisational renaissance.

flags.arabic: ويتلخص بيان الاتحاد الذي أصدره بخصوص ثورات الربيع العربي فيما يلي: 1- … 7- …
options: display with the attribution to the Union made unmistakable
display as an ordinary news item
flags.note: CRITICAL — critical_for_display. The seven points are the news desk's summary of a communiqué issued by a body of thirty people. They are not the Sheikh's words, not his positions, and not even the communiqué's own wording. He is named in the first sentence as one participant. On a page carrying his name, in English, a numbered list of positions on the Arab Spring will be read as his. The English keeps 'the Union' as the subject throughout, but the site's layout must not undo that. Anyone wanting the Union's actual text needs the communiqué itself, linked from the record.

flags.arabic: بوصفه عضوا في الاتحاد … الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين
flags.context: the Sheikh's membership of the Union, stated in the first sentence
options: translate faithfully and hold for an editorial decision
flags.note: editorial_review, on grounds of the record's consequences rather than its content. The record states the Sheikh's membership of a named international body. That body has since been the subject of terrorism designations by several states, including the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Bahrain — a matter of public record, stated here neutrally and without any view as to its merits. Republishing in English, under Ummah Collective's name, a record whose first sentence establishes that membership is a decision with consequences for him and for the publisher in some jurisdictions, and it belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office, not to the translator. Nothing has been softened or omitted; the membership is stated exactly as the Arabic states it.

flags.arabic: 3- ينبغي للذين يتهيؤون للمناصب القيادية … أن يتقوا الله
flags.context: the third point of the communiqué
options: ought to be mindful of God
it is recommended (mandūb) that they be mindful of God
flags.note: ينبغي is ordinary normative Arabic, not the technical mandūb of the five-rulings table, and this is a communiqué's exhortation rather than a ruling issued by a jurist about an act. Option 3 would manufacture a ruling. Recorded because ينبغي is frequently and wrongly mapped onto 'recommended' in translations of this literature.

flags.arabic: من سنن الله ونواميسه في الكون / سنة التدرج
options: God's established patterns and laws in the created order
the sunnahs and norms of God in the universe
flags.note: سنن الله here are the regularities God has set in creation, not the sunnah of the Prophet; the same term as in record 770 in this span, and it needs the same fixed rendering. Leaving 'sunnahs' in the English would be read the other way by most readers. نواميس is its near-synonym and is kept distinct as 'laws'.

The Arabic is bare and does not say plurality of what. In a December 2011 communiqué on the Arab uprisings the political sense is likely, but 'pluralism' in English is a political doctrine and 'political pluralism' names it outright; both would resolve something the Arabic leaves open, and the following clause grounds it in creation rather than in politics. 'Plurality' is kept as the least committal. A reviewer with the communiqué itself can settle it.

translator_notes: A news report summarising a communiqué. No part of it is by the Sheikh, and no ruling is stated anywhere in it, so the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is not engaged.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written. The body dates the meeting to 3–4 December 2011, a week before the timestamp.
الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين is rendered by the body's own English name, the International Union of Muslim Scholars.
ترشيد الأمة is rendered 'to guide the community rightly'. The verb is from rushd, right guidance, and 'to rationalise' — the word a dictionary offers — would be a false friend here.

The closing 'to see the final communiqué click here' is the site's navigation furniture. The link is external, to iumsonline.org, and is recorded in source_download_link; it is not a dedewnet asset and may well be dead.
